_note: Plain-English definitions shown when a reader taps a term in a story summary or the 30-second panel. Keep each to one or two short sentences, with no figures that go out of date. 'case': true means match the exact capitalisation (for acronyms). 'also' lists other spellings that should show the same definition.

terms.def: A group of mostly central, eastern and southern EU countries that want to protect EU money for poorer regions (cohesion funds) and farming in the bloc's budget.
The interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends money to banks for short periods. When it goes up, loan and EMI rates usually follow.
The Monetary Policy Committee: the RBI panel that votes on the repo rate.
Consumer Price Index: tracks the prices of a basket of everyday goods and services. Its yearly rise is the main measure of retail inflation.
Wholesale Price Index: tracks prices at the wholesale level, before goods reach shops.
Gross domestic product: the total value of the goods and services an economy produces.
The gap between what a government spends and what it earns. It covers the gap by borrowing.
An Indian unit equal to 10 million, or 100 lakh.
An Indian unit equal to 100,000.
Minimum support price: the price at which the Indian government says it will buy certain crops from farmers.
An index of 50 large companies listed on India's National Stock Exchange (NSE), used as a gauge of the whole market.
An index of 30 large companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
An index of the biggest bank shares listed on the National Stock Exchange.
A measure of how much traders expect the Nifty to swing over the coming month. Higher means more nervousness.
Initial public offering: when a company first sells shares to the public and lists on a stock exchange.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission, which regulates US stock markets and listed companies.
The main global benchmark price for crude oil, based on oil from the North Sea. India's oil import costs track it closely.
West Texas Intermediate: the main US benchmark price for crude oil.
A group of oil-exporting countries, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, that agrees how much oil its members pump.
The narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman. A large share of the world's oil and gas shipments pass through it.
An armed group that controls much of northern Yemen, including the capital, Sanaa.
A tax on imported goods, paid by the company bringing them in. It is often passed on to buyers as higher prices.
A US trade law that lets the government put tariffs on a country after an investigation finds it treats US business unfairly.
A US trade law that allows tariffs on imports judged to threaten US national security.
The International Emergency Economic Powers Act: a US law that gives the president economic powers during a declared national emergency. It was used to impose broad tariffs.
Penalties, such as trade bans or frozen assets, that a country imposes on another country, a company or a person.
Government rules that restrict selling certain goods or technology, such as advanced chips, to other countries.
A forum of the world's major economies whose leaders meet once a year.
The clause in NATO's founding treaty that lets any member call for talks with the others when it feels threatened.
NATO's mutual-defence clause: an armed attack on one member is treated as an attack on all.
Air Quality Index: one score for how polluted the air is, combining several pollutants. Higher is worse. India's scale runs from 'good' to 'severe'.
Tiny particles in the air, less than 2.5 micrometres across, that can reach deep into the lungs.
Graded Response Action Plan: Delhi-NCR's anti-pollution curbs, in stages that get stricter as the air gets worse.
The Commission for Air Quality Management, which decides when GRAP stages start and end in Delhi and nearby areas.
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation: India's aviation safety regulator.
The Federal Aviation Administration: the US agency that runs air traffic control and regulates aviation safety.
An air traffic control order that keeps flights on the ground, usually until a problem is fixed.
A formal letter from a regulator asking a company to explain why action should not be taken against it.
A legal order to hand over documents or to appear and give evidence.
When the US Congress does not approve funding in time, many federal agencies stop non-essential work and some staff are sent home.
A stopgap US law that keeps the government funded at existing levels for a set time.
US elections held halfway through a president's four-year term, for all House seats and about a third of the Senate.
The lower house of India's Parliament, directly elected by voters.
The upper house of India's Parliament, mostly elected by state legislatures.
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act: the Indian law that controls how charities and other groups receive money from abroad.
An AI model whose trained weights are published, so anyone can download and run it, even if its training data and code are not.
How much text an AI model can take in and consider at once.
An AI model that works through a problem step by step before answering. It is usually slower but better at maths and code.
The Federal Communications Commission, the US regulator that licenses radio spectrum and satellite networks.
Adjusted gross revenue: the part of a telecom company's income that India uses to calculate the fees it owes the government.
The band of space closest to Earth where satellites circle the planet quickly. Being close means less delay for internet signals.
The military version of SpaceX's Starlink, sold to governments. The US government buys it for Ukraine's armed forces.
A ground station with large antennas that links satellites to the regular internet.
